title: fix(ui): refresh agent identity after Gateway file saves
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Open Control UI tabs could retain an old name or avatar after `IDENTITY.md` was saved through a Gateway file RPC. The connection-scoped identity cache introduced in #167968 had no notification for those writes.

## User Impact

Successful identity-file saves through `agents.files.set` and `sessions.files.set` refresh open chats, the roster, and forwarded avatars. Idle identity reads remain suppressed. Direct filesystem/shell edits still require reload or reconnect; native clients retain their existing catalog-loading behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

The file RPCs publish `agent.identity.changed` only after a committed write. Session-file saves match the configured agent workspace's exact identity path, excluding unrelated project and nested files. Before publishing, the writer drains any older identity-file read so an immediate client refresh cannot join a stale in-flight result. The existing UI identity owner handles invalidation and stale-response rejection.

The obsolete TTL assertions reported by CI are already corrected on the main base. This PR adds the missing production notification path and its boundary regressions. The file-write tests use the existing real-storage fixture; the oversized mutation suite shrinks.

Non-test LOC delta: **+43**, needed for the write/event contract and read ordering. No new polling loop, cache, config option, module, export, or schema change.

## Evidence

- Run `37999811982`, head `f8239ea9470d13d70cd222d992b79582604db816`, jobs `114055137248` and `114055137269`: four stale-TTL assertions. Blacksmith Testbox `tbx_01m4hesfbrtm9b3xjfdqz8qn18` reproduced all four (149 other tests passed, 4.89 s). The added identity-event browser case failed on the original consumer.
- Linux Node 24.19.0, CI UI configuration and three workers: the original failing files plus identity tests passed **three repetitions, 169 tests each** (8.12 / 4.53 / 4.41 s). Five bundled Chromium cases passed in 36.34 s. Over **10 virtual idle minutes**, there was **one bootstrap identity read and zero additional reads**, versus 11 before #167968. Announced drain added zero identity/catalog/cron reads.
- AWS Crabbox `cbx_8d08927d2d6d`: 7,051 UI sibling tests across 495 files passed (three skips); 221 Gateway tests across 13 files passed (11 skips). The one-worker `pnpm test <files> --maxWorkers=1` batch passed in 26.63 s for Gateway files and 7.74 s for UI files.
- Authorized Linux rig, pinned source and Node 24.19.0: the relocated file-RPC batch passed **72 tests in 39.29 s** with `pnpm test src/gateway/server-methods/agents-files.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/agents-mutate.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`. Fourteen GNU-shell cases were conditionally skipped because the host uses uutils; no remote-shell coverage is claimed. The local-disk negative control fails on the original code and observes committed bytes when repaired.
- Core, core-test, and UI typechecks; ownership/format/protocol/i18n guards passed. Three unrelated dead-export findings also fail on the unchanged base and are fixed by #168048, now included by rebase. Final-head dead-export scans pass with zero entries; targeted source lint and all 1,339 script files pass. Remaining structural checks and final-head Gateway/browser smoke tests pass. Previously passing full type/ownership checks were reused across the unchanged feature patch; the final rebase adds the canonical dead-export repair.
- Independent Codex review: clean through P2. Final aggregate review of commit `14189fde0588c58d37e3ab90be1593d5ed0f9821`: clean through P2.

Validation used synthetic browser data and isolated temporary state, with no production Gateway or live channel account. Before/after screenshots show Atlas/🦞 becoming Cedar/🌻 while preserving the unsent draft and session.

Final-head smoke: all five bundled-browser cases passed in 58.37 s. The original full type-check batch, final-head dead-export scan, targeted source/style/script lint, and remaining structural guards all passed.
